live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a Rust-based ransomware-as-a-service tied to hospital, casino and council attacks
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, rents out ransomware to affiliates. It surfaced in November 2021, drew FBI and State Department attention, and its leak sites went down in 2023 and 2024. Many victim claims are the gang's own.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
Malpedia describes it as a ransomware-as-a-service family written in Rust. It has been seen in attacks since 18 November 2021.
BleepingComputer reports that ALPHV is believed to be a rebrand of the DarkSide and BlackMatter operations.

Cisco Talos has moderate confidence that BlackMatter affiliates were probably early BlackCat adopters. A BlackCat representative said the two groups were connected but that BlackCat was not a rebranding.
S2W found that BlackCat's configuration fields matched BlackMatter's. It still found it difficult to conclude they were the same group.
eSentire says various security teams report that the core operators are based in Russia. The eSentire report does not verify this itself.
Malpedia lists a US Justice Department release of 30 December 2025. It says two Americans pleaded guilty to targeting US victims with ALPHV BlackCat ransomware.

The FBI linked the gang to over 60 breaches in its first four months, from November 2021 to March 2022. BleepingComputer reports the FBI estimates at least $300 million in ransom payments from more than 1,000 victims up to September 2023.
Reported victims include a Louisiana city, the pharmaceutical firm Sun Pharmaceuticals and the dental supplier Henry Schein.
The gang also listed the lender loanDepot and the insurer Prudential Financial on its leak site. BleepingComputer notes these claims were unverified because no proof had yet been published.
The gang claimed to have taken more than 1 TB from Constellation Software. It claimed more than 130 GB from Estée Lauder. Both figures are the gang's own claims.
Malpedia says the ransomware can encrypt files with AES or ChaCha20. It can delete volume shadow copies, stop services and ESXi virtual machines, and spread across a network using PsExec.

Symantec describes updates in mid-2022. They added an ARM build, safe-mode encryption and indexing of stolen data on leak sites. An affiliate was also seen using the Eamfo infostealer against Veeam backup credentials.
CrowdStrike lists Alphv among the ransomware-as-a-service platforms used against VMware ESXi in early 2023.
In a 2023 Sygnia case, attributed to BlackCat or one of its affiliates, access came through a compromised third-party vendor. The attacker used Cobalt Strike and Rclone, then sent extortion emails.
eSentire reports that ALPHV affiliates used Google ads to lure users into downloading Nitrogen, an initial-access malware that led to ALPHV ransomware.
In its own statement on MGM Resorts, AlphV said it launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors on 11 September 2023. These claims are unverified.

BleepingComputer cited unnamed sources linking the Change Healthcare attack to BlackCat. It could not confirm this, and BlackCat had not claimed the attack at the time. UnitedHealth's SEC filing described a suspected nation-state actor.
The gang's Tor negotiation and leak sites were disrupted in December 2023, according to BleepingComputer.

In March 2024 BleepingComputer concluded the gang was running an exit scam. The gang told the outlet its infrastructure had been seized. Europol and the NCA said they were not involved in any recent disruption.
DataBreaches reported that AlphV claimed an employee at Viking Therapeutics filed an SEC complaint after an attack. DataBreaches described the breach as unconfirmed.
Defenders can reduce risk by locking down vendor access, remote-management tools and backup credentials, and by keeping offline backups.
